name: Qube Browser 0.1.16-alpha
notes:
Splitscreen, second pass

The first version put two pages side by side. This one makes the split behave
like something you can use all day.

- The divider between two panes now drags. Take hold of the gap and the panes
  resize with it; neither can go below 240 pixels wide. The bars, the pill and
  the focus outline follow the pointer as you drag.
- The gap shows your Space's own gradient, and it changes with the theme
  picker.
- Clicking into the other half now lands the first time. It used to take two.
- You can scroll a half without clicking it first.
- The pointer becomes a text cursor over text and a hand over links in both
  halves, and dragging out a selection stays inside the half it started in.
- The outline around the half you are working in follows your clicks, and it
  keeps a visible edge whatever colour the theme is.
- The two halves line up exactly. A one-pixel step between them is gone.
- Each half's bar matches the Mac layout: copy, address and menu travel
  together as one centred group, with the close on its own at the right.

Splits in the sidebar

- A split is one row, the same height as a tab row, and it drags as one unit.
  Drop a tab onto it to join.
- Right-click gives Pin Split and Unpin Split, and a pinned split comes back
  as a split after a restart.
- If you pinned a split before this build, it was saved as two separate pins
  and will stay that way. Split and pin it once more to fix it.

Elsewhere

- In Mac style, clicks on a single page no longer land 32 points off.
- A page's rounded corner no longer shows a grey edge where the card met it.
- A page that declares no colour of its own is handled as exactly that,
  instead of guessing.
- A pane bar keeps its text readable when you hover it, and the close cross is
  gone when there is only one pane to close.

Known

- Dragging the divider still does not feel as immediate as it should. The
  panes follow, but the motion lags the pointer. Being worked on.
- Navigating away from a split has once left the old page on screen. If you
  see it, say so.
- Which half you were working in is not remembered across a restart; the
  outline returns to the left one.
- On Windows the halves have no hairline edge of their own yet, the way they
  do on Mac.
- You still cannot make a split by dragging a tab onto the page, nor by
  Alt-clicking a link. Right-click a tab and choose Split Right.
- A split restored from a previous session appears once you click either half.
- In Mac style, hovering the green dot does not open Windows' snap-layout
  menu. Windows style keeps it.
- A download does not yet say which site it came from.
- An extension popup still takes about a second to appear.
summary: Splitscreen, second pass: the divider between two panes now drags, and the split handles clicks, scrolling and selection the way it should.
